answer: Require each agent identity to post a refundable bond before it can transact, sized to the value it wants to move. Reputation then accrues only from completed, verified work, a slow nectar no one can buy in bulk, and it decays when idle, so a fresh sockpuppet starts at zero while a long-lived identity risks real money if it cheats. Cheap quartz-like proof-of-work puzzles gate account creation, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs more in compute and locked capital than any single fraud can recover. The fable of free identities ends: every new face pays to play and earns trust over time.
